newsitem.title: USA: Florida consumer confidence hits eight-year high.
newsitem.headline: Florida consumer confidence hits eight-year high.

text.p: Florida's consumer confidence index hit an eight-year high in July amid optimism about the national economy, University of Florida economists said Tuesday.
The index rose two points in July to 101, the highest level since June 1989, a year before the beginning of the last recession.
"People seem to be telling us that they are doing fine and anticipate continued growth," said Chris McCarty, survey director for the school's Bureau of Economic and Business Research.

Florida's confidence index has risen by 10 points in the last year. Two-thirds of survey respondents said they expect good times to last into the next century. Eighty-three percent expect no recession in the coming year, up from 73 percent a year ago.
Consumer debt service payments have begun to level off after nearly four years of steady increases, McCarty said.

Two of the five indicators that make up the index rose last month. Consumers perceptions that now is a good time to buy big-ticket items rose four points to 116. Consumers' expectations about the national economy over the next five years rose by six points to 85.
Optimisim about current finances fell four points, to 91 in July from 95 in June.

The share of respondents claiming business was better than a year ago increased three points to 53 percent. The share expecting extra employees to be hired at their workplace in the next six months increased one point, to 37 percent in July.
On the negative side, car sales fell in June, down sharply from a year ago, and retail sales rose only 0.5 percent in June after a weak first quarter in 1997.
And while discount department stores are enjoying greater sales, inventory is piling up at high-end department stores.
The monthly index was calculated from a telephone survey of 866 randomly selected adult Floridians and has an error margin of three percent.
